Salehurst Church of England Primary School
What an amazing Healthy Living Week we've had! Throughout the week, our children enjoyed a variety of exciting activities designed to promote healthy lifestyles. They got hands-on by making their own delicious, healthy wraps and were curious to taste a range of vegetables, with many discovering some new favourites! There was plenty of opportunity to keep active too! The giant inflatables, including the assault course and mega slide, were a huge hit as you can see by the smiles. Children also enjoyed fantastic cricket sessions led by coaches from Robertsbridge Cricket Club, who volunteered their time for us, where they developed lots of new skills and practised their teamwork. Our skipping workshops were another highlight, with children mastering new tricks and challenging themselves throughout the sessions. We rounded off the week with a special Sports Day morning adapted to better suit the hot weather and ensure everyone stayed safe while still enjoying a fun-filled morning of races, teamwork and encouragement. We were so proud of the resilience, determination and sportsmanship shown by all our pupils this week. A huge thank you to everyone who helped make Healthy Living Week such a memorable success. We hope the children have been inspired to continue making healthy choices and staying active throughout the summer!

pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care - breakfast and after school clubs
Wraparound Care Procedures and Charging Policy
5:20 Club - Our after school provision, known as the 5:20 Club, is very popular and a great facility for children whose parents are unable to collect them at the end of the day. The club is open to all ages and runs from Monday to Friday, 3.30 to 5.20 pm. The children enjoy a range of activities including art and craft, games, puzzles, computers, gardening and outdoor play. Miss Knight co-ordinates the club, with support from other staff. The costs can be found in the Terms and Conditions document above.
Please speak to Miss Knight, either by email, salehurstwcare@thebridgefederation.org or in person at school, if you would like more information.
Breakfast Club - this runs daily from 8:00 am - A healthy breakfast is served, ie wholegrain cereals, wholemeal toast/muffins/bagels plus fruit juice or milk. Costs can be found in the Terms and Conditions above.
Please speak to Miss Knight, either by email, salehurstwcare@thebridgefederation.org or in person at school, if you would like more information.

PE and Sport Premium
Please read the information below which gives details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.
At Salehurst Church of England Primary School we aim to provide enriched sporting provision, both through excellent PE teaching and through the appropriate level of competitive sporting opportunities.
We also sign up to The Hastings & Rother School Games Partnership (HRSGP) annually and from this receive both high quality pupil and staff training in PE/Sport and competitive opportunities in a range of events. School Sports Coordinator, Jane Dallaway from Robertsbridge Community College delivers Sports Leader training and inter school sports competitions in the Robertsbridge Cluster, which Salehurst attends. These range from Cross Country, Netball, Football, Sports Hall Athletics, Badminton, Gymnastics, Multi skills, Basketball, Cricket, Swimming and Quad Kids Athletics. This gives many different pupils the opportunity to represent the school and over the last 2 years has ensured Salehurst have received the “Gold” School Games Mark, a nationally recognised award for the delivery of high quality PE/Sport.
We welcome the Government's additional PE & Sports Funding for Primary Schools, please see the document below for guidance as to how this funding has been used at our school.

pageCache.text:
Late/Absence Procedures & Guidance on Children's Health
We understand that it can be tricky deciding whether to keep your child off school when they are unwell. For most common childhood illnesses and infections (including coughs and colds) schools follow these government and NHS guidelines, which set out when a child should be kept off school and when they shouldn't: Should I Keep My Child Off School and Is My Child Too Ill For School. The new Pharmacy First service is also available to help with some common conditions without the need for a GP appointment, and the poster below gives more details. Please phone or email the school office if you would like any support with your child's attendance.
If your child is going to be absent from school for any reason please let us know no later than 9am on the first day and on any subsequent days, by doing one of the following:
This email is checked early in the morning when the registers are taken.
Medical Appointments
As you will be aware we ask parents to try and make routine medical and dental appointments for after school or during the school holidays, to minimise any disruption to learning. However we appreciate that sometimes this is not possible. When an appointment has to be made for during the school day please can you supply us with some form of confirmation (appointment card, letter, email, etc). This is necessary for us to accurately record the absence in the class register, which is a legal document. If you do not have written confirmation of the appointment please ask the office for a Medical Absence form to complete. Thank you for your cooperation with this.
Email salehurstschool@thebridgefederation.org.

pageCache.pageTitle: Salehurst Church of England Primary School - Our Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
We believe that our most important task is to equip children with the skills and knowledge for their future, reaching far into the C21. We celebrate the present, are fascinated by the past and, in learning about both, we invite the children to wonder at what lies ahead. How will these citizens shape the world for the better?
We follow the Revised National Curriculum 2014 and have developed an integrated Long Term Plan to best meet the needs of learners in our school. This is flexible in design and teachers enjoy reviewing and reinventing units of learning. As one half of The Bridge Federation, we follow our own separate Curriculums but share ideas and resources for two out of three terms. A development we are working on is to share our Summer Term topic across both schools in all year groups; this summer the theme will be ‘Woodlands’. This enables cross fertilisation of ideas and hopefully creates opportunities for the children to mix and learn together too.
Our quality curriculum ensures sound learning progress. Each class experiences a broad and balanced set of topics across a year, often with a Humanities or Science focus. We value all the expressive arts and appreciate the impact on children’s spiritual development if they can dance, paint and act out their understanding of the world. We use an enquiry based approach, fostering the children’s sense of curiosity. Our four Learning Powers (Resilience, Resourcefulness, Reflectiveness and Relationships) help the children develop their self-awareness and skills as independent learners.
We value all the pupils in our school equally and believe that each child is entitled to experience success by having their needs met and supported.
Post-COVID, we reintroduced the whole curriculum straight away, aiming to give the children back their enthusiasm for learning while also maintaining a raised awareness of supporting their emotional development. This aim continues, as we have realised that the impact of COVID is still with us.
In the Summer term, we seek to create an immersive experience for our children across the school, with each class taking a different direction in terms of curriculum design and objectives covered within the same theme. The topics will enable all children to learn from their environment around them locally and wider.
Further detail for each topic can be found on our Class Pages.
Should you have any questions surrounding our school curriculum, please direct them to the school office.
